calls.reason: This is a hedged belief with no deadline. SoftBank's October disclosure of $30 billion in completed investment weighs against imminent collapse, but does not settle the analogy.

Reuters reports both a stalled-plan allegation and Huang's denial. The staged $100 billion intention and smaller proposed round contribution do not clearly establish whether Nvidia materially pulled back.

Fortune reports large operating losses in both 2024 and 2025, and WSJ reports company projections placing profitability in 2030. Together they support the main point of continuing losses and profitability years away, despite missing quarterly results.

Engadget reports a $122 billion round including Amazon and new individual investors, with Nvidia and SoftBank committing $30 billion each. Reported secondary-market weakness was not linked to the investor retreat Marcus predicted.

February 10 Reuters reporting explicitly describes growing investor concern about financing OpenAI's commitments. MoneyWeek's December coverage and reports of doubts about the Nvidia deal corroborate increasing scrutiny.

SoftBank disclosed completing $30 billion in investment in October, so the funding-cutoff condition is not established. TechCrunch's executive departures do not demonstrate flight to competitors following a cutoff.
